statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-mode audit of the public unauthenticated entry, listing, media detail, search, age/consent flow, and failure-state surface.

page.framework: server-rendered multi-page site with jQuery/Vue components
page.notes: A mandatory age gate precedes content. The audited entry flow dismissed it and exercised the essential-only consent path. Authenticated account, payment, upload, and playback completion were not covered because they require credentials, payment, or extended media interaction.

artifacts.caption: Metadata, links, controls, forms, and document probe
Preferences, CSS features, focus, permissions, and auth probe
Lighthouse performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated dark screenshot plus CSSOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark and default screenshots are pixel-identical in appearance and size (63,936 bytes), while the CSS probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, document.getAnimations() returned no active animations, so no non-essential load motion remained to suppress.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse axe plus emulated contrast probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse axe color-contrast audit passed, and text and controls remained present under prefers-contrast: more.
The age-gate dismissal and cookie-wall arrival occur as an abrupt state swap in the interaction video; CSS inspection found no view-transition rules.
No parallax, scrollytelling, or entry/exit reveal interaction was present on the audited entry and representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, or entry/exit reveal interaction was present on the audited entry and representative templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No swipe, pull, carousel, or other gesture-driven control was present on the audited entry flow.
checkOutcomes.reason: No swipe, pull, carousel, or other gesture-driven control was present on the audited entry flow.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The long listing exposes static navigation chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress affordance.
The audited overlays are full-page age/consent dialogs, not anchored tooltips or edge-positioned menus.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited overlays are full-page age/consent dialogs, not anchored tooltips or edge-positioned menus.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The age notice places a single prominent heading and two explicit age choices in a centered modal, clearly directing the required next action.
After the mandatory age gate is dismissed, a second full-content cookie wall immediately obscures the page, as shown by the transition contact sheet.
The visible age modal is a DIV with role=dialog/aria-modal rather than a native dialog; the platform probe found no dialog or popover primitive.
The first viewport is visually restrained: branding, one heading, explanatory copy, and the required age actions dominate, with no application frame crowding the notice.
At 360x800, layout reported scrollWidth 360, clientWidth 360, and 0 px horizontal overflow; the viewport meta is present.
The site renders reused card/modal components across desktop and mobile, but CSSOM inspection found no @container or container-type support, leaving adaptation viewport-bound.
Programmatically focusing the first visible link produced outline-style none and no box shadow, so keyboard focus is not visibly indicated.
The entry viewport states that this is an adults-only site and exposes explicit enter and exit actions without requiring exploration.
The recorded flow dismissed the age gate and exposed the consent choices, including an equally visible essential-only option; the core entry path advances predictably.
A deliberately nonexistent URL returned HTTP 200 and the generic site shell rather than a truthful 404 state, making failure indistinguishable from success.
Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 14.1 s, FCP 3.0 s, and interactive 14.1 s (performance 0.64), well outside a good load experience.
The 360x800 layout observer recorded CLS 0.1021 from a shift at about 1.59 s, just above the good threshold.
The trace recorded zero long tasks and 0 ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT was 90 ms.
The load made 170 requests and transferred 5.08 MB; seven parser-inserted stylesheets and multiple non-deferred scripts were confirmed as high-priority render-blocking candidates.
Lighthouse estimated 177 KiB unused JavaScript and 74 KiB unused CSS, including two mobile stylesheets about 97% unused.
Lighthouse axe passed button-name, link-name, image-alt, and landmark checks; the image primitive found zero missing alt attributes.
Lighthouse axe color-contrast passed with no violating nodes.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse structure checks plus focus probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Although heading order and landmarks passed, the active keyboard target had no outline or box shadow, so focus is not always visible.
The age-notice heading and body text are large, high-contrast, centered, and readable at desktop and mobile widths without clipping.
Lighthouse found user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0 in the effective mobile viewport meta, preventing user zoom despite target-size passing.
Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading addEventListener) in setInstallButton on initial load.
Doctype/UTF-8 and aspect ratios were sound, but the image audit found three images without explicit dimensions and 33 without responsive srcset.
Lighthouse found two deprecated behaviours and four BFCache failure reasons, including a main-frame unload handler and cache-control:no-store.
The public home page title is only Pornhub and the direct DOM probe found no meta description, providing little page-specific context.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse SEO and direct robots fetch
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) thumbnail links and treated robots.txt as HTML with 4,067 parse errors; mobile zoom is also disabled.
Although a canonical URL exists, the public home page declares noindex,nofollow and /robots.txt returns a 458 KiB HTML page instead of a valid robots policy.
The listing page contains no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite representing a browsable media collection.
HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are missing; cookie rp is not Secure and all seven cookies use SameSite=None.
The initial load contacted 12 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and DoubleClick; 99 third-party requests transferred 2.05 MB before entry.
No geolocation or notification prompt fired on load, and the page ships a dedicated passkey module and passkey banner while exposing PublicKeyCredential.
HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff are absent.
The non-JavaScript fetch is not an empty shell, but discoverability coverage is only 28% and the crawler view loses most rendered listing content.

checkOutcomes.method: Responsive screenshots, layout, and flow video
checkOutcomes.evidence: The age and consent overlays remained contained at desktop and 360 px mobile widths with no horizontal overflow, and the essential-only path remained operable.
This streaming media service is intrinsically online; an offline/installable experience is not required for its core content.
checkOutcomes.reason: This streaming media service is intrinsically online; an offline/installable experience is not required for its core content.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A guaranteed nonexistent route responded 200 with the general shell rather than a distinct error and recovery state.
The Polish page declares html lang=pl, and Lighthouse validates the language code; the localized age notice renders in Polish.
No dates, currencies, durations requiring locale formatting, or editable locale-sensitive values were present in the audited entry flow.
checkOutcomes.reason: No dates, currencies, durations requiring locale formatting, or editable locale-sensitive values were present in the audited entry flow.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited entry, listing, search, and media-detail surfaces expose no scheduled event or time-zone-sensitive user data.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited entry, listing, search, and media-detail surfaces expose no scheduled event or time-zone-sensitive user data.

checkOutcomes.method: Flow contact sheet and desktop screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent wall presents Accept All, Accept Only Essential, and Customize choices together with comparable visual weight; the age gate provides explicit enter and exit actions.
The audited public flow contains only a non-required search input; no required data-entry form was present to validate or recover.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public flow contains only a non-required search input; no required data-entry form was present to validate or recover.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The only public input is site search, for which address, payment, sign-in, and identity autofill tokens do not apply.
checkOutcomes.reason: The only public input is site search, for which address, payment, sign-in, and identity autofill tokens do not apply.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The public entry exposes sign-in without forcing it, ships passkey support, and does not force a purchase or continuity commitment in the audited flow.
Of 37 images, 25 use legacy formats and 33 lack srcset; three lack dimensions, increasing avoidable transfer and layout cost.
The entry load makes 170 requests and ships 251 KiB of estimated unused JS/CSS before the user clears the age and consent gates.
Ninety-nine third-party requests transfer 2.05 MB, with TrafficJunky ads alone over 1 MB and known analytics trackers active before entry.
No agent-facing capability is declared or expected for this public media-browsing surface; the emerging WebMCP opportunity was judged out of scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing capability is declared or expected for this public media-browsing surface; the emerging WebMCP opportunity was judged out of scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation, generation, or other user task on the audited entry flow calls for on-device inference.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation, generation, or other user task on the audited entry flow calls for on-device inference.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten repeated language-wrapper state toggles, heap node count fell from 557,599 to 557,238 and self size fell from 37,489,626 to 37,209,370 bytes, with no retained-growth signal.
The pre-entry page retained 557,599 heap nodes and 37.5 MB self size before the user reached content, a high footprint for an age gate and listing shell.
Across the repeated state-toggle comparison, total heap nodes decreased by 361 rather than accumulating; no aggregate detached/listener-growth symptom appeared in the tested window.

principleOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing capability is declared or expected for this public media-browsing surface; the emerging WebMCP opportunity was judged out of scope. No summarisation, generation, or other user task on the audited entry flow calls for on-device inference.

paths.description: Public home/age-gate entry and consent flow; represents global chrome and initial load.
Video listing template discovered from primary navigation; inspected through rendered DOM and shared gate.
Representative non-explicit safety-training media detail linked from home; covers detail metadata/player template.
Search results for safety; covers the primary discovery form and result template.
Public sign-in route/auth surface probe; used to inspect passkey and form signals without credentials.
Guaranteed nonexistent route; covers HTTP/error recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The fixed dark palette does not honour the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Dark and default screenshots are pixel-identical in appearance and size (63,936 bytes), while the CSS probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and preference-driven surface tokens with light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: The age-to-consent state change is abrupt.
findings.evidence: The age-gate dismissal and cookie-wall arrival occur as an abrupt state swap in the interaction video; CSS inspection found no view-transition rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a same-document View Transition for the gate dismissal, while disabling it under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long-page navigation does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The long listing exposes static navigation chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll-state-aware header or progress/scrollability cue without JS scroll handlers.

findings.summary: Two consecutive full-content gates interrupt access on every fresh session.
findings.evidence: After the mandatory age gate is dismissed, a second full-content cookie wall immediately obscures the page, as shown by the transition contact sheet.
findings.suggestedFix: Combine required disclosures where legally possible and use a compact, persistent, non-blocking consent surface after the mandatory age decision.

findings.summary: The modal flow uses custom DIV dialogs instead of native dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The visible age modal is a DIV with role=dialog/aria-modal rather than a native dialog; the platform probe found no dialog or popover primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, showModal(), cancel handling, focus return, and platform dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Reusable components rely only on viewport styling.
findings.evidence: The site renders reused card/modal components across desktop and mobile, but CSSOM inspection found no @container or container-type support, leaving adaptation viewport-bound.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and modal sections containment and adapt them with size container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on the first interactive target.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focusing the first visible link produced outline-style none and no box shadow, so keyboard focus is not visibly indicated.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline that is not removed, and verify it across all controls.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return a misleading successful shell.
findings.evidence: A deliberately nonexistent URL returned HTTP 200 and the generic site shell rather than a truthful 404 state, making failure indistinguishable from success.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status with a localized message, search/home actions, and preserved navigation.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is 14.1 seconds.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 14.1 s, FCP 3.0 s, and interactive 14.1 s (performance 0.64), well outside a good load experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element and its dependency chain, prioritize it, and defer non-critical scripts, ads, and below-fold work.

findings.summary: Mobile CLS reaches 0.102.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout observer recorded CLS 0.1021 from a shift at about 1.59 s, just above the good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late banners/assets and stabilize font and image geometry.

findings.summary: The entry transfers 5.08 MB through 170 requests with a long blocking chain.
findings.evidence: The load made 170 requests and transferred 5.08 MB; seven parser-inserted stylesheets and multiple non-deferred scripts were confirmed as high-priority render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, reduce duplicate document/XHR delivery, and cache immutable assets.

findings.summary: The entry ships about 251 KiB unused JS/CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 177 KiB unused JavaScript and 74 KiB unused CSS, including two mobile stylesheets about 97% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific bundles and conditionally load analytics, billing, login, and below-fold component code.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visible.
findings.evidence: Although heading order and landmarks passed, the active keyboard target had no outline or box shadow, so focus is not always visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a consistent :focus-visible treatment and test a complete keyboard focus walk.

findings.summary: The viewport disables pinch zoom.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0 in the effective mobile viewport meta, preventing user zoom despite target-size passing.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; retain width=device-width, initial-scale=1.

findings.summary: Initial load throws in setInstallButton.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading addEventListener) in setInstallButton on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the queried install button before adding listeners and cover the absent-button state in tests.

findings.summary: Several images omit dimensions and responsive sources.
findings.evidence: Doctype/UTF-8 and aspect ratios were sound, but the image audit found three images without explicit dimensions and 33 without responsive srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio and provide srcset/sizes for raster thumbnails.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload/Cast patterns and BFCache blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two deprecated behaviours and four BFCache failure reasons, including a main-frame unload handler and cache-control:no-store.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/fetchLater where appropriate, use disableRemotePlayback, and remove avoidable no-store blockers.

findings.summary: The page lacks descriptive, page-specific title and description metadata.
findings.evidence: The public home page title is only Pornhub and the direct DOM probe found no meta description, providing little page-specific context.
findings.suggestedFix: Write a localized descriptive title and meta description for each template.

findings.summary: robots.txt is invalid HTML and several cards use javascript:void(0) links.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) thumbnail links and treated robots.txt as HTML with 4,067 parse errors; mobile zoom is also disabled.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid text/plain robots.txt and replace pseudo-links with real crawlable href values.

findings.summary: Public indexing signals conflict through noindex/nofollow and malformed robots.txt.
findings.evidence: Although a canonical URL exists, the public home page declares noindex,nofollow and /robots.txt returns a 458 KiB HTML page instead of a valid robots policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide the intended indexing policy, then align HTTP status, robots.txt, robots meta, canonical, sitemap, and localized hreflang signals.

findings.summary: The media listing has no structured or social metadata.
findings.evidence: The listing page contains no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite representing a browsable media collection.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and appropriate schema.org JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: Core security headers are missing and one cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are missing; cookie rp is not Secure and all seven cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP in report-only then enforce it, add nosniff, mark every cookie Secure, and tighten SameSite where cross-site use is unnecessary.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising run before entry across 99 third-party requests.
findings.evidence: The initial load contacted 12 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and DoubleClick; 99 third-party requests transferred 2.05 MB before entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics/ads until consent, reduce vendors, batch telemetry, and document each third party.

findings.summary: Referrer, permissions, CSP, and nosniff defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, CSP frame-ancestors/Trusted Types where compatible, and X-Content-Type-Options.

findings.summary: Only 28% of rendered content matches raw HTML.
findings.evidence: The non-JavaScript fetch is not an empty shell, but discoverability coverage is only 28% and the crawler view loses most rendered listing content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful listing and navigation content, keeping JavaScript as enhancement rather than the source of crawler-visible state.

findings.summary: Missing routes return HTTP 200 with no truthful recovery state.
findings.evidence: A guaranteed nonexistent route responded 200 with the general shell rather than a distinct error and recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct failure status and a localized, actionable error page with retry/search/home options.

findings.summary: Most thumbnails use legacy formats without responsive sources.
findings.evidence: Of 37 images, 25 use legacy formats and 33 lack srcset; three lack dimensions, increasing avoidable transfer and layout cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes and preserve intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Substantial network and unused code runs before consent and core access.
findings.evidence: The entry load makes 170 requests and ships 251 KiB of estimated unused JS/CSS before the user clears the age and consent gates.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential code and requests, split by template, and defer below-fold/ad work until needed.

findings.summary: Third parties consume 2.05 MB before entry.
findings.evidence: Ninety-nine third-party requests transfer 2.05 MB, with TrafficJunky ads alone over 1 MB and known analytics trackers active before entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, delay ad/analytics media until consent and visibility, and remove low-value vendors.

findings.summary: The pre-entry heap footprint is disproportionately large.
findings.evidence: The pre-entry page retained 557,599 heap nodes and 37.5 MB self size before the user reached content, a high footprint for an age gate and listing shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load content, advertising, account, and billing modules after the gate and release hidden modal/listing state.

taskList.title: Stop pre-consent third-party loading and reduce the 5 MB/170-request entry path
Restore keyboard focus visibility and user zoom
Fix indexing: valid robots.txt, real links, metadata, and aligned robots signals
Deploy a complete defensive header and cookie baseline
Improve LCP/CLS and remove unused or blocking code
Replace stacked custom modal interruptions with semantic, calmer disclosure UI
Return truthful, recoverable HTTP error states
Clean up platform errors, deprecations, BFCache blockers, and responsive assets
Server-render more meaningful listing content for no-JS clients
Add component-level and scroll-aware responsive behavior
